newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal's Somincor puts new plan to miners.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's Somincor puts new plan to miners.

text.p: Portuguese state-owned company Somincor presented a new plan to copper workers on Wednesday which would boost the number of holidays in return for Sunday working at the Neves Corvo mine.

Personnel director Raul Araujo told Reuters that the plan met the terms of the outline deal done with miners in the early hours of last Saturday morning and which put an end to a five-day stoppage at the mine, 250 km south of Lisbon.
The company had agreed then to present a detailed proposal on Wednesday which miners would then vote on on Thursday.
The deal was struck after government officials joined talks in a bid to break a deadlock which had shut the 107,000 tonnes per year mine, Europe's largest.

Somincor said that miners would be entitled to 104 days off a year, including 26 Sundays, compared with the 91 free days and 13 Sundays it had intended when it initially sought to introduce Sunday shifts.
It was the introduction of Sunday working the sparked the strike.
Asked how he rated the company offer, union leader Eduardo Lazaro said that the company's first idea had been "very bad" and that the latest was "distinctly less bad."
Somincor says that continuous shifts are essential if the mine is to remain competitive because ore yields are declining.
